newsitem.title: USA: Kodak sees Japan dispute continuing.
newsitem.headline: Kodak sees Japan dispute continuing.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co chairman George Fisher said Monday the company may be embroiled in a dispute over opening the Japanese photo film market for 18 more months.
"Sooner or later we're going to break it open," Fisher told the Council of Institutional Investors at a conference here.
He said he expects a World Trade Organization panel soon to take up Kodak's complaint that the Japanese market unfairly favors Fuji Photo Film Co Ltd.

"Now we'll find out whether the WTO actually has the teeth that it's supposed to have ... We'll probably be in this for another 18 months before we get a final result. And then the Japanese, who are masters at slow rowing, they'll take their cozy time about making any real changes," he said.
Fisher said he has little concern about a request recently filed by Japan seeking an inquiry into the competitive structure of the U.S. photo film market.
In an interview after his remarks, Fisher confirmed that talks are continuing between Kodak and Wang Laboratories Inc concerning the possible acquisition of Wang's imaging unit by Kodak.
"We're in discussions with Wang about their imaging software business," Fisher told Reuters.
But he declined to comment on reports that Wang is seeking a price of $250 million to $300 million for the unit.
